fields.justification: The evidence bundle closes over approval records.
The evidence bundle closes over the artifacts it validated.
The evidence bundle closes over assumption records.
The evidence bundle names the exact compile-result attempt it supports so same-attempt closure is machine-checkable; the compile result reciprocates via evidence_bundle_ref.
The evidence bundle closes over conflict records.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
Contract validation must prove it did not read credentials.
The evidence bundle closes over default records.
The evidence bundle closes over derivation records.
The evidence bundle closes over diagnostic records.
The bundle must include the exact frozen IR target version its mappings validate against.
The evidence bundle closes over IR v0.1 gap records.
The evidence bundle needs a stable, unique identity like every other record.
Evidence is content-addressable; the input digest anchors it to exact validated bytes.
The evidence bundle closes over the mapping records naming accepted requirements and IR pointers.
The evidence bundle closes over model-proposal records.
Contract validation must prove it did not access the network.
The evidence bundle closes over open-question records.
Every requirement must appear in the bundle's mapping evidence.
Validation result must include every schema hash within the evidence bundle's closure.
The evidence bundle closes over the exact source evidence its accepted requirements reference.
The evidence bundle closes over planned test/evidence mapping records.
Validation evidence reports schema inventory/hashes, fixture outcomes, and determinism.
Simple, Developer, API, file, and future PRS producers must converge on one contract while remaining attributable.
Authoritative inputs are named explicitly so lower-ranked input cannot silently supply meaning.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
The authoring envelope needs a stable identity that requirement documents can reference.
The versioned intent is part of the authoritative input boundary.
Non-authoritative input is preserved as evidence and can never govern.
Every authority/default decision behind a mapping must identify its controlling clause and evidence.
A no_ir_representation mapping must carry its stable diagnostic; the schema requires it conditionally on that outcome.
Missing IR representation requires stable Phase 5 gap evidence.
Every mapping record needs a stable, case-sensitive, unique identity.
Direct, derived, defaulted, unresolved, prohibited, and missing representation are materially different.
A mapping is a machine-readable edge from a stable requirement identity to its outcome.
Successful IR mappings must identify an exact RFC 6901 pointer into frozen IR v0.1.
A mapping's validation evidence must be an immutable, content-addressable record.
A requirement must map to planned test/evidence IDs proving its meaning, or record an explicit unresolved evidence obligation.
Proposed, accepted, unresolved, disputed, unsupported, refused, and invalid meaning cannot be conflated.
Approval evidence is conditional on consequential meaning and must be explicit, attributable, and scoped.
Every accepted claim needs visible authority, and lower-ranked authority cannot silently override it.
Consequential meaning invokes approval and fail-closed rules.
Default-derived meaning must identify the visible, attributable, authorized default record.
Stable identity is required for evidence and cross-reference integrity.
Required versus optional meaning controls terminal status, and required meaning cannot silently become optional.
No requirement may exist without attributable source evidence.
The accepted or disputed meaning must remain explicit; only a change to this semantic unit can create a new requirement identity.
Classification makes completeness and policy checks deterministic.
The machine-stable RQC code carries diagnostic meaning.
Each diagnostic record needs a stable identity.
Messages are parameterised presentation keyed by a stable identifier.
Parameters carry machine meaning alongside the code.
A diagnostic identifies the related requirement identities when available.
Severity is stable per code and drives deterministic ordering.
A diagnostic identifies the related source evidence when available.
Approval identifies the deciding authority.
The exact decision, including revocation and expiry, is preserved.
Approval requires attributable evidence; silence and UI state are not approval.
An approval record needs a stable identity.
Approval is exact-scope and machine-readable so scope coverage can be checked.
An immutable sequence orders approval evidence deterministically.
Approval is linked to the exact requirement, default, or operation it authorises.
Assumption acceptance state cannot be collapsed into accepted meaning.
A consequential assumption requires explicit approval and cannot be applied silently.
Consequential assumptions invoke approval and fail-closed rules.
A canonical assumption needs a stable identity so assumption_refs can close over it.
An assumption states whether it affects required or only optional meaning.
An assumption identifies the source evidence it was drawn from.
The assumed meaning must remain explicit.
Assumptions are explicit records preserved in the canonical document.
A conflict preserves the authority level of each claim so precedence stays visible.
A conflict preserves all competing claims rather than one chosen interpretation.
A conflict record needs a stable identity.
A conflict names every affected requirement.
Unresolved required conflicts block; resolution state must be explicit.
A conflict preserves the sources behind each claim.
Conflicts are preserved with all claims rather than normalised away.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
A default links to each requirement it affects.
A consequential default requires explicit owner or user approval evidence.
Approval state is recorded; it is derived from a resolved approval record and is never self-certifying.
A default identifies the authority that permits it.
Consequential defaults invoke approval thresholds.
A default record needs a stable identity.
A default is authorised only within its exact declared scope.
A default carries its supporting source evidence.
A default is never applied invisibly; its meaning is stated.
A derivation record needs a stable identity.
A derivation identifies all inputs.
A derivation identifies all outputs.
A derivation is permitted only by a stable contract clause it names.
A derivation carries deterministic validation evidence.
The requirements document needs a stable identity for result and bundle references.
The document names the exact authoring input it was produced from.
Model output holds proposal authority only and may never be accepted.
A model proposal needs a stable identity.
A proposal preserves its prompt/input digest.
A proposal preserves its output digest.
A proposal names the records it proposed so model-originated meaning stays attributable.
A proposal preserves its source references for validation against real evidence.
Ambiguity is preserved as an open question rather than silently resolved.
A question identifies the requirement meaning it blocks.
A canonical question needs a stable identity so question_refs can close over it.
A question states whether it blocks required meaning or only an optional item.
A resolved question must carry the evidence that resolved it.
Resolved and unresolved questions are materially different and cannot be conflated.
The unresolved ambiguity is preserved verbatim as a question.
The requirements document is part of the explicit output boundary.
Accepted meaning requires attributable source evidence carried in the document.
A test mapping needs a stable identity.
Every accepted requirement maps to planned test/evidence identifiers.
Planned, satisfied, and unresolved evidence obligations are distinct.
Each validation attempt is a new immutable record with a stable identity.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
Non-success results carry sorted, machine-readable diagnostic references.
The compile result references the evidence bundle that closes over its supporting records.
A result must reference the exact mapping records that name its accepted requirements and IR pointers.
Stable sorted diagnostics explain non-success without prose parsing.
The compile result is one of the explicit cross-referenced parts of the output boundary.
Terminal outcomes must be explicit and machine-distinct.
A source assertion is evidence, not implicit authority.
Stable source identity prevents silent evidence substitution.
Producer surfaces remain attributable while converging on one contract.
Current, missing, replaced, and withdrawn evidence have different validity; replacement links old and new source IDs without deleting old evidence.
Exact URI and JSON Pointer are preserved byte-for-byte and support reproducible diagnostics.
A replaced source must link to its replacement so old evidence is preserved rather than deleted.
Byte-backed sources require content identity; ephemeral claims may lack bytes.
